title: Deeper/broader downstream DWG claim boundary and cross-peer loss-mode review
mode: primary project-documentation and public issue-body review; plan-only update
scope: Separate LibreCAD 3 downstream DWG product direction from library-level implementation capability
Cross-check recent peer reader/writer failure reports for transferable regression-method lessons
Map reported failure modes to existing PAR owners without treating peer reports as local defects
Preserve the fast local validation cadence and external evidence boundary

method.kind: Read current public project policy and exact peer issue reports; reconcile against the local plan
method.limitations: LibreCAD_3 master documentation and peer issue pages are mutable. Reports are author-provided and were not reproduced; the linked pinned vendored ledger, issue attachments, exact peer binaries, and source branches were not independently acquired or run. No report establishes a local libdxfrw defect or normative format rule.

sources.observed: The app document states optional, off-by-default DWG import through libdxfrw; DWG writing is not implemented/exposed/planned absent explicit gates. It describes 15 pinned reader claims (11 EXPERIMENTAL, 4 PENDING_NATIVE), no PROMOTED claims, common integrity/target-debt blockers, and no write-direction claims. This is product-policy documentation, not an inspection of the vendored ledger bytes or an enduring policy guarantee.

sources.revision: Open issue reports reviewed 2026-10-18; reported versions differ by issue
sources.observed: Reports describe recursive repeated-DXF paths causing stack exhaustion, a VERTEX subtype placeholder causing an AC1014 document-build failure, an AC1032/AutoCAD 2025 MTEXT-flag file rejection whose cause remained unproven after entity bytes matched, and silent 3DSOLID/REGION omission from an ACadSharp DWG-to-DXF writer. These are peer-specific reports, not normative behavior or libdxfrw failures.

sources.revision: Issue pages reviewed 2026-10-18; mutable master is not treated as a release
sources.observed: Reports describe an unresolved entity reference terminating a DXF layout, an outer loop index mutation skipping later block bodies, and an INSERT attribute-follow flag without required child/SEQEND records. The #1351 issue notes a later master fix for its exact reproducer. None demonstrates a matching libdxfrw defect.

assessment.planImpact: Clarifies LibreCAD_3's current read-only product contract separately from library capability; reinforces local progress/bounds, per-source disposition, per-owner graph closure, whole-file native acceptance, and exact-version attribution under existing PAR-14/PAR-26, PAR-22/7H, PAR-49/7G, PAR-59, and transaction/output-closure owners.

implementationReadyChecks: Keep library capability separate from LibreCAD_3's optional read-only DWG product path and do not infer an app-side write claim.
For changed parser loops, use bounded generated repeated-record cases, explicit progress/resource assertions, and a following-record sentinel; peer crash thresholds are not format limits.
For changed writer traversal, reconcile every source identity to one emitted or explicit refusal disposition and close block/INSERT/ATTRIB/SEQEND ownership.
For PAR-59 ACIS output, preserve full inline payload sequence and entity/block/INSERT reachability before semantic-consumer testing.
Treat unresolved peer reports and native failures as exact-version hypotheses; do not adopt an unverified recovery rule or infer causes from object-byte equality alone.

Keep each implementation slice on touched-target strict build, focused selector, compatibility compile when public/shared contracts change, and owning CTest; composed peer/native qualification stays one-time and optional.
Keep J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 DEFERRED_EXTERNAL unless their required independent evidence is actually obtained.
